article.body_html:
A monthly rental only works if the bike has somewhere to sleep every night. In an apartment block, whether a bike may be kept there is up to the landlord or the building management, not you, and the answer can be a flat no, a place in a basement, a tag to buy or a yard that is locked at a set hour. Ask before you commit to the month, not after the bike is standing at the gate.

Questions for the landlord or the building management

Ask the buildingWhy the answer matters
May a rented bike be parked here, or only bikes owned by residents?A rule written for owners can leave a rental bike with no place
Where exactly: a basement, a ground-floor yard or outside?It decides how sheltered the bike is overnight and how easily you can reach it
Is a card, tag or ticket needed, and who issues it?Without it the gate may stay shut to your bike
Is there a monthly fee, who collects it and what receipt is given?A fee agreed by voice is hard to prove later
Who controls the gate, and at what hours is it open?A gate that is locked late at night or early in the morning can strand a bike or a rider outside
Does anyone supervise the parking, and what happens if a bike is damaged or taken there?The answer tells you how much to rely on the building and how much protection to ask about
Does the spot fit this bike, and may you add a lock or a cover?A cramped spot is a risk for both the bike and the bikes around it

Ask them in person if you can, and write down each answer the same day. If the landlord is not the person who runs the parking, ask for that person's name and number, because they are the one who will open the gate.

Why the rental shop needs to hear about it too

The bike belongs to the shop, so the shop may have views on where it is kept overnight and on locks. Put it to the shop as a question (+84 334 699 969, 09:00–21:00 daily): "The bike will be kept in an apartment block, in this place. Is there anything you need me to do about locks or about where it stays?" If the shop asks for the address or a photo of the spot, you can give them once you have the building's permission. A parking routine with locks is described in rental bike locking in Hanoi.

Get the building's answer in writing

A message from the landlord or the management counts for more than a nod at the door. Ask for one that names the bike (or says "a rented motorbike"), the place, the fee if there is one and the gate hours. Then photograph the spot, the card or tag when you get it, any notice of the gate hours and the receipt for any fee. If the building later disagrees with what you remember, the photos and the message are your side of the story.

If the answer is no

  • Look for paid parking nearby. Ask neighbours and the landlord where residents leave their bikes, and visit the place before you rely on it.
  • Ask about a different bike. If space is the problem, ask the shop whether a smaller bike is an option; how to choose the right bike covers the choice more widely.
  • Ask whether the arrangement can change, for example a fee in return for a spot, or a different position in the yard.
  • Reconsider the month. A bike that has no safe place to stay overnight is a poor fit for a monthly rental, however good the price.

If a staffed car park will keep the bike, record who has the keys before you leave it, and for a hotel stay the questions in overnight motorbike parking in Hanoi overlap with the ones above.

Before you commit to the month

  1. Have the building's answer in writing.
  2. Have the shop's answer about locks and about where the bike stays.
  3. Know the fee, who collects it and the hours of the gate.
  4. Walk the route from the parking place to your door, in the dark if you will use it then.
  5. Only then confirm the month with the shop, starting from its monthly motorbike rental page.
